name: LiveFlow
description: It pipes QuickBooks, bank, and revenue data into a spreadsheet that refreshes itself, for planning, consolidations, and dashboards. Redwood City. Founded 2021. Not bootstrapped.

mentions.evidence: Growjo estimates about $6.7 million a year as of September 2025, with 52 employees, and that estimate is also shown on GetLatka. The company has not published revenue.
mentions.indieAngle: One report, refreshed into a sheet, for a fixed monthly fee. Thirteen weeks of cash, or a profit-and-loss across several companies.

whyItPrints: Accountants are not leaving the spreadsheet. They will pay for a spreadsheet that is less stale.
whyThisMatters: A finance person will not abandon the sheet. LiveFlow sends QuickBooks, the bank, and revenue numbers into Google Sheets or Excel, and the sheet updates itself, for a forecast, a consolidation, or a dashboard. Redwood City. Founded in 2021, and it is not a bootstrap. Growjo estimates about six point seven million a year as of September 2025, with fifty-two employees, and GetLatka shows the same estimate. The company has not published revenue. I am not treating a data site as their books. A narrower version is one report on a timer. Thirteen weeks of cash, or the profit and loss of several companies, refreshed into a sheet for a flat monthly fee. The accountant keeps the tool they already trust. GetLatka is showing the Growjo estimate, not a second measurement that happens to match. One guess, printed in two places. The headcount sits on that same estimate. A 2021 start means the guess covers a short life, and they took outside money. The sheet is the product because that is where the accountant already works, whether the job is a forecast or several companies added together.
